doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Leaving the show after two years; subs who could not play stride
summary: He tired of the show after about two years and the producers resisted his outside tours; his substitutes' stride was fake.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How long did it take you to decide, “I’ve had enough of this?”

About a year and a half. Actually, about two years. I had had enough. I told them, their nose used to get out of joint when you had to leave the show. I told them when I joined the show, "I have to do this tour in Japan. I have to go to Europe. I have to do such and such date." They said, "okay, we don't mind." Then, when it became time for me to go out and do that, they objected.
Who subbed for you when you did that?
Leonard something…I forget his last name.
So they found you a sub.

Yes, they found one. In fact, at one point found a girl to sub in for me. But, she could not play stride. She played fake stride. When I was doing the show, I played authentic stride on piano. You had to do it. Sometimes, one of those things was a
handful of keys. It was a tempo about here (taps very fast tempo). You had to play that kind of stride. It got easier as it went on.
